info.title: lucentAPI
info.description:
An HTTPS API for lucentBASE, for lucentLIMS and any other client.

**Authentication.** Send an access token from the OpenID Connect provider as
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The token's username has to belong to a person in lucentBASE
(`person.unix_account`); every change is recorded under that person.

**Roles** come from the token: `sampler` registers collections, `analyst` records values,
`reviewer` accepts them (never their own: four-eyes principle), `admin` may do everything.
Reading needs no role.

**Audit trail.** Every write adds a row to the table's log table (`l_<table>`), chained by
SHA-256 checksums.

**Concurrent changes.** Records that can be changed carry an `etag`. Send it in `If-Match`;
if the record changed meanwhile, the answer is 412.

**Errors** look like `{"error": {"code", "message", "request_id", "details"?}}`.

**Times** are UTC.

get.description: No token needed. Fails with 500 if the database can't be reached.
The person behind the token and the roles it grants.

schema.title: Response Reference Systems V1 Crs Get

get.description: Sites with address and border. WKT stores (longitude latitude); the border is converted.

schema.title: Response Collection Classes V1 Collection Classes Get

get.description: Actions (methods) with what they measure, their devices, people and dependencies.
Newest first. Status is derived from the values, so filtering by it reads every match.

post.description: Registers a collection. Its identifier comes from the numbering scheme and its id.

get.description: A collection with all its values.

post.description: Records a reading. A further reading of the same variable becomes the next repetition.
Accepts a value. Not allowed for whoever measured it (four-eyes principle). Honours If-Match.
Takes back the acceptance of a value. Honours If-Match.
Accepts all values of a collection, or none if the caller measured any of the open ones.

get.description: Values of many collections at once, oldest first, for clients that keep a local copy.
One numeric variable over time at a spot or site: the last repetition per collection.
